items.title: mg to mcg: a simple conversion
items.description: 1 mg equals 1,000 mcg. Multiply mg by 1,000, or divide mcg by 1,000. Our free converter shows both units. Mass conversion only; it does not choose an amount to take.
items.prerequisite: Verify the connected BACwater account, channel rules and live destination before publication.
items.altText: Mass conversion reference: 1 mg equals 1,000 mcg; 0.125 mg equals 125 mcg.

items.title: U-100 units and mL: know the difference
items.description: On a U-100 scale, 100 units equals 1 mL. A scale reading is not a mass in mg or a product amount in IU. Our free converter checks the arithmetic. Verify the actual device scale.
items.prerequisite: Verify the connected BACwater account, channel rules and live destination before publication.
items.altText: U-100 scale reference: 100 units equals 1 mL; 25 units equals 0.25 mL.

items.title: What does mg/mL mean?
items.description: Concentration is mass divided by final solution volume. In this arithmetic example, 12 mg in a final volume of 4 mL equals 3 mg/mL. Our calculator uses your own numbers. This is not a preparation instruction.
items.prerequisite: Verify the connected BACwater account, channel rules and live destination before publication.
items.altText: Concentration example: 12 mg divided by a final volume of 4 mL equals 3 mg per mL.

items.title: mg to mcg explained: milligrams and micrograms
items.description:
One milligram equals 1,000 micrograms. This 32-second visual guide explains the relationship and works through 0.125 mg = 125 mcg.
